about: How loud each part is rendered (registry/README.md): every modelled instrument's audio set from its measured sound power, so that the parts stand to one another as the instruments do.

stem-level.about: A modelled part's audio level from its instrument's sound power (public/shared/performers/sound-power.js stemLevelDb; sound-power.json, TU Berlin's anechoic database, Weinzierl et al. 2017): its held notes' RMS, dBFS, as it enters its player's channel, its sound power level in dB re 1 pW plus the reference.

reference.reason: the loudest instrument measured, the tuba, at its ff (112.3 dB at its median pitch) 18 dB under full scale, so that a section of brass at ff stays under each player's limiter (audio.js BOT_LIMITER, past its channel's +3.7 dB) and its fff high in its compass reaches it; the bowed strings' violin at ff then 5 dB under where its model stood before (8 October 2026: -37.54 dBFS, its stem gain matched to its recordings)

velocity-law.about: How a velocity, 0 to 1, is heard as an amplitude within a family's dynamic range (audio.js familyVelocityGain, planned-dynamics.js velocityAtDb): its amplitude a power of a line from the range's floor to full scale.

exponent.reason: a velocity's amplitude rising as the square of a line through the family's range where its family names no other (Dannenberg 2006's square law, which matches commercial synthesizers' velocity curves within a chosen range in dB)
